html:
Túpac Katari was an Aymara leader who led a great revolt against Spanish rule in 1781 and besieged La Paz for months. He was executed by being pulled apart by horses.

Born Julián Apaza, he was a trader in coca and cloth. In early 1781, during the rising of Túpac Amaru II in Peru, he raised tens of thousands of Aymara fighters against the mita, forced sales of goods and abusive officials. With his wife Bartolina Sisa, he laid siege to La Paz for over 100 days, and many in the city died of hunger.

Spanish troops broke the siege, and he was betrayed and killed in November 1781. His words were remembered as "I will return as millions". He became the symbol of the Aymara movement of the 20th century, the Katarista movement, and of the rise of Evo Morales in Bolivia.
sum: Túpac Katari was an Aymara leader who led a great revolt against Spanish rule in 1781 and besieged La Paz for months. He was executed by being pulled apart by horses.
